claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy has an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
The untreated as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy exhibits a sharp, hysteretic magnetostructural transition.
Controlled laser surface modification will refine the near-surface grain structure and increase grain-boundary density.
Controlled laser surface modification will introduce localized near-surface strain fields.
The laser treatment can produce the proposed microstructure without changing the overall alloy composition.
Heat treatment or processing can substantially affect lattice strain and grain size.
A high defect density can produce a broad distribution of exchange parameters and magnetically inhomogeneous behavior.
Nanostructured grain boundaries and heterogeneous localized strain facilitate distributed nucleation and growth during the magnetostructural transition.
Distributed transformation kinetics make the magnetostructural transition more gradual.
The laser-induced microstructure will broaden the magnetic entropy-change profile relative to the untreated baseline.
The laser-induced microstructure will reduce magnetostructural hysteresis relative to the untreated baseline.
Laser treatment will cause a modest shift in the transition temperature.
Increasing internal grain-boundary area increases the effective surface-to-volume ratio relevant to heat exchange.
The laser-treated samples will exchange heat more rapidly during thermal cycling.
The predicted broadening and hysteresis reduction will persist under low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The predicted effects require the laser treatment not to compromise mechanical stability.
